definitions.sampling_outcome_or_later_recovery_expos: Include an event when its sampling/recovery record explicitly reports later status/outcome/implementation metadata or substantive post-initial draft exposure. This conservative union includes later draft content even without a formal acceptance label. Current title/date enumeration alone, retained-but-unshown payload fields, and the initial Draft header alone are not sufficient.
definitions.sampling_explicit_status_only: Narrow descriptive subset: a positive later-status field or later_status_metadata_seen flag. Q05/Q06/Q07 are separately retained as later-recovery-draft exposures, not invented formal outcomes.
definitions.strict_any_recorded_current_status_follo: Union sampling, common and A/B records for the event. Include recorded current proposal or related predecessor/companion/followup snippets, implementation-status/release-change text, later design bodies and explicit later-behavior references, even when not opened or used as evidence. Do not count mere delivery/storage without recorded display, current page date alone, generic catalog names or link labels without relevant proposal/status context. This intentionally broad set does not assert a positive outcome for the sampled proposal.
definitions.opposite_route_input_exposure: Positive saved record that an executing A or B selector saw the other route's route-specific input, result, candidate selection or judgment before its own return. Authorized common baseline reuse, same-route batch input, same-worker cross-question memory, scheduling completion notices and the later exposed audit are separate.
definitions.exact_component_overlap: Same concrete component/use and operational role in the prior inventory and returned candidate. Shared upstream project, language, generic pattern or hosting domain alone does not qualify.
definitions.exact_document_overlap: Compare original returned citation URLs to prior cited document URLs, lowercasing scheme/host and removing fragments. A separate query-stripped check is also reported. Do not silently equate editions, commits, different files or same-host projects.
definitions.broader_provider_family_overlap: Same identifiable upstream project family (e.g. Go or Bazel), although the concrete component/document/use differs. Hosting domains such as github.com, docs.rs or pkg.go.dev, language ecosystems and broad standards affiliations do not by themselves establish a shared supplier project.
